title: Professional YouTube Script
description: Generate a structured, retention-optimized script for a YouTube video, complete with hook, chapters and a call to action.
prompt:
You are an experienced YouTube scriptwriter. Write a complete video script about "[TOPIC]" for a channel aimed at "[AUDIENCE]".

Structure the script as:
1. Hook (first 15 seconds) — a bold claim, question, or surprising fact that stops the scroll.
2. Intro (15-30s) — tell viewers exactly what they'll learn and why it matters.
3. Main content — break into 3-5 clearly labeled chapters/timestamps, each delivering one concrete idea with an example.
4. Recap — summarize the key takeaways in one short paragraph.
5. Call to action — ask viewers to like, subscribe, or comment with a specific question.

Keep the tone conversational, use short sentences, and flag places where I should add a visual or B-roll cue in [brackets]. Target length: about [LENGTH] minutes of spoken content.

title: Code Review Assistant
description: Turn any AI model into a thorough, constructive code reviewer that flags bugs, style issues and security risks.
prompt:
Act as a senior software engineer performing a code review. I will paste a code snippet or diff below.

For the code I share, respond with:
1. **Summary** — one sentence on what the code does.
2. **Bugs & correctness issues** — anything that could break at runtime or produce wrong results, with the exact line referenced.
3. **Security concerns** — injection risks, unsafe input handling, secrets in code, etc.
4. **Readability & style** — naming, structure, or formatting improvements, following [LANGUAGE/FRAMEWORK] conventions.
5. **Suggested refactor** — a short rewritten version of the most important fix, in a code block.

Be direct and specific. Don't rewrite the entire file unless I ask — just show the parts that changed. Here is the code:

[PASTE CODE HERE]

title: SEO Blog Post Outline
description: Produce an SEO-friendly outline for a blog post, including target keywords, headings and meta description.
prompt:
You are an SEO content strategist. Create a detailed outline for a blog post targeting the keyword "[PRIMARY KEYWORD]" for an audience of "[AUDIENCE]".

Include:
- A compelling, keyword-rich title (under 60 characters)
- A meta description (under 155 characters) that encourages clicks
- 5-8 H2/H3 headings that follow a logical reading flow
- 2-3 bullet points of what should be covered under each heading
- 3-5 secondary/LSI keywords to weave in naturally
- One suggested internal linking opportunity and one external authoritative source to cite
- A recommended word count based on top-ranking competitor content

Do not write the full article yet — outline only.

title: Cinematic Portrait Prompt
description: A reusable template for generating cinematic, editorial-style portrait images with consistent lighting and mood.
prompt: cinematic portrait of [SUBJECT DESCRIPTION], [AGE] years old, [EXPRESSION/MOOD], soft rim lighting from the left, shallow depth of field, shot on 85mm lens at f/1.4, film grain, muted color grade with teal and orange accents, editorial photography style, ultra-detailed skin texture, background softly blurred showing [SETTING], shot like a still from an A24 film --ar 2:3 --style raw --v 6

title: Product Explainer Video Storyboard
description: Break a product idea into a shot-by-shot storyboard ready to feed into an AI video generator.
prompt:
Act as a video director. I want a 30-second product explainer video for "[PRODUCT NAME]", which does "[ONE-LINE VALUE PROP]".

Create a shot-by-shot storyboard with 6-8 shots. For each shot, give me:
- Shot number and duration (in seconds)
- Camera framing (close-up, wide, over-the-shoulder, etc.)
- What's happening on screen
- Suggested on-screen text or voiceover line
- Mood/lighting notes

The pacing should build from a relatable problem, to the product as the solution, to a clear call to action in the final shot. Keep voiceover lines under 12 words each so they read comfortably at normal speaking pace.

title: Exam Concept Simplifier
description: Turn a dense textbook concept into a simple explanation with an analogy and a practice question.
prompt:
You are a patient tutor. I'm studying for an exam on "[SUBJECT]" and struggling with the concept of "[CONCEPT]".

Please:
1. Explain it in plain language, as if to a curious 15-year-old.
2. Give one real-world analogy that makes it click.
3. Show a short worked example.
4. Write one practice question at the same difficulty as my exam, then wait for my answer before revealing the solution.

Avoid jargon unless you define it immediately.

title: Literature Review Synthesizer
description: Summarize and compare multiple papers or sources into a structured mini literature review.
prompt:
You are a research assistant helping with a literature review on "[RESEARCH TOPIC]".

I will paste summaries or abstracts of several sources below. For each one, extract:
- Main claim/finding
- Methodology (sample size, method type)
- Key limitation the authors acknowledge

Then write a short synthesis paragraph that:
- Identifies where the sources agree
- Identifies where they disagree or contradict each other
- Points out a gap in the current research that could be a study idea

Sources:
[PASTE ABSTRACTS/SUMMARIES HERE]

title: Weekly Priorities Planner
description: Turn a messy brain-dump of tasks into a prioritized weekly plan using a simple urgent/important framework.
prompt:
Act as a productivity coach. Below is an unsorted list of everything on my plate this week.

Organize it using this process:
1. Sort every item into one of four buckets: Do Now (urgent+important), Schedule (important, not urgent), Delegate (urgent, not important), Drop (neither).
2. For the "Do Now" and "Schedule" buckets, suggest which day of the week (Mon-Fri) each task fits best, assuming I have about [HOURS] focused hours per day.
3. Flag any task that looks unrealistic to fit this week and suggest what to push to next week.

Here is my list:
[PASTE TASK LIST HERE]

title: Startup Pitch Deck Feedback
description: Get investor-style critique on a pitch deck outline, slide by slide.
prompt:
You are an experienced venture capital investor who has reviewed thousands of pitch decks. I'll describe my deck slide by slide; give me candid feedback as if I were pitching to you live.

For each slide I describe, tell me:
- What's missing that investors expect to see on that slide
- One question the current version would raise in an investor's mind
- A sharper way to phrase the key claim

At the end, give an overall gut-check: would this deck get a second meeting, and why or why not?

Here are my slides:
[DESCRIBE EACH SLIDE — PROBLEM, SOLUTION, MARKET SIZE, BUSINESS MODEL, TRACTION, TEAM, ASK]

title: Cold Outreach Email
description: Draft a short, personalized cold email that gets replies instead of getting ignored.
prompt:
Write a cold outreach email to "[RECIPIENT ROLE]" at "[COMPANY]" about "[REASON FOR REACHING OUT]".

Rules:
- Under 120 words total.
- Open with something specific about them or their company, not a generic compliment.
- State the value to them in one sentence, not a feature list.
- End with a low-friction ask (a yes/no question, not "let's hop on a call").
- No corporate jargon like "synergy" or "circle back".
- Write a subject line under 6 words that would make me open it.

title: Debugging Rubber Duck
description: A structured 'rubber duck debugging' prompt that forces you to explain the bug clearly before getting a fix.
prompt:
Act as a rubber duck debugging partner. I'll describe a bug I'm stuck on. Before suggesting any fix, ask me clarifying questions one at a time until you understand:
- What I expected to happen
- What actually happened
- What I've already tried
- The smallest piece of code that reproduces it

Only after that, propose a hypothesis for the root cause and one small experiment I can run to confirm it, before giving me the actual fix.

Here's the bug:
[DESCRIBE THE BUG]

title: App Icon Concept Set
description: Generate a set of clean, modern app icon concepts for a mobile product.
prompt: minimalist app icon design for a [APP CATEGORY] app called "[APP NAME]", flat vector style, single bold symbol representing [CORE FEATURE], rounded square container, two-tone color palette of [COLOR 1] and [COLOR 2], soft gradient, subtle drop shadow, no text, iOS app icon grid, clean and modern, product design mockup on a plain background --ar 1:1 --v 6

title: Short-Form Video Hook Generator
description: Generate a batch of scroll-stopping hooks for TikTok/Reels/Shorts on a given topic.
prompt:
You are a short-form video strategist. Give me 10 different hook lines (first 3 seconds of spoken/on-screen text) for a video about "[TOPIC]" aimed at "[AUDIENCE]".

Use a mix of these hook styles, labeling which style each one is:
- Contrarian statement
- Curiosity gap / open loop
- Bold numbers or stat
- "Nobody tells you..." angle
- Direct callout of the viewer's problem

Keep each hook under 12 words so it fits on screen in large text.

title: Meeting Notes to Action Items
description: Convert raw, messy meeting notes into a clean summary with clear owners and deadlines.
prompt:
Turn the raw meeting notes below into a clean recap. Output in this format:

**Meeting summary:** 2-3 sentence overview of what was discussed.

**Decisions made:**
- List each decision as one line.

**Action items:**
- [Owner name] — [task] — [deadline if mentioned, otherwise write "TBD"]

**Open questions:**
- Anything left unresolved that needs a follow-up.

Here are the raw notes:
[PASTE MEETING NOTES HERE]

title: Competitor Analysis Snapshot
description: Build a structured comparison of your product against named competitors on key dimensions.
prompt:
Act as a market research analyst. Compare "[YOUR PRODUCT]" against these competitors: [COMPETITOR 1], [COMPETITOR 2], [COMPETITOR 3].

For each competitor, summarize:
- Positioning (one sentence on how they market themselves)
- Pricing model
- Their strongest feature / differentiator
- Their weakest point or common user complaint

Finish with a short paragraph on where "[YOUR PRODUCT]" has a real opening to differentiate, based on the gaps above.

title: Essay Thesis Strengthener
description: Pressure-test an essay thesis statement and suggest sharper, more arguable versions.
prompt:
You are a writing tutor who specializes in argumentative essays. Here is my thesis statement:

"[PASTE THESIS STATEMENT]"

1. Tell me honestly whether it's actually arguable, or if it's just a statement of fact.
2. Point out any part that's too vague or too broad to defend in one essay.
3. Suggest 3 sharper, more specific versions of the thesis that would be easier to argue convincingly.
4. For your favorite version, list 3 supporting points I'd need to prove it.

title: Regex Explainer & Builder
description: Get a working regular expression built from a plain-English description, with a line-by-line breakdown.
prompt:
Act as a regex expert. I need a regular expression that matches: "[DESCRIBE WHAT YOU WANT TO MATCH]" and does NOT match: "[DESCRIBE WHAT SHOULD BE EXCLUDED]".

Give me:
1. The final regex pattern in a code block, for [LANGUAGE/FLAVOR, e.g. JavaScript, PCRE, Python re].
2. A plain-English, token-by-token breakdown of what each part does.
3. Three example strings that should match and three that shouldn't, to test against.

title: Study Schedule Builder
description: Create a realistic, spaced-repetition-friendly study schedule leading up to an exam date.
prompt:
Act as a study coach. I have an exam on "[SUBJECT]" on [EXAM DATE]. I need to cover these topics: [LIST TOPICS]. I can study about [HOURS] hours per day, [DAYS PER WEEK] days a week.

Build a day-by-day study schedule that:
- Front-loads the topics I find hardest (I'll tell you which ones if asked)
- Uses spaced repetition — revisit each topic at least twice before the exam, not just once
- Includes 1-2 full practice-test days in the final week
- Leaves the last day light, for review only, not new material

Ask me which topics are hardest before building the plan.

title: Survey Question Designer
description: Turn a research goal into a set of unbiased, well-structured survey questions.
prompt:
You are a survey methodology expert. I want to learn: "[WHAT YOU WANT TO LEARN]" from "[TARGET RESPONDENTS]".

Design a survey with 8-10 questions that:
- Starts with 1-2 easy screening/demographic questions
- Uses a mix of question types (multiple choice, Likert scale, one open-ended)
- Avoids leading or double-barreled questions
- Ends with one open-ended question that could surface an insight you didn't think to ask about

For each question, briefly note what insight it's designed to capture.

title: Daily Standup Summarizer
description: Turn your own rough notes into a clean, concise daily standup update.
prompt:
Turn my rough notes below into a clean async standup update in this exact format:

**Yesterday:** what I completed, in 1-3 bullet points.
**Today:** what I'm focused on, in 1-3 bullet points.
**Blockers:** anything slowing me down, or "None" if there aren't any.

Keep the whole thing under 80 words, written in first person, no fluff.

My rough notes:
[PASTE ROUGH NOTES HERE]

title: Brand Voice & Tone Guide
description: Define a reusable brand voice guide so every future piece of copy sounds consistent.
prompt:
Act as a brand strategist. Based on the description of my brand below, create a brand voice guide with:

1. Three adjectives that describe the voice (e.g. "witty, direct, warm") with one sentence explaining each.
2. A "we say / we don't say" table with 5 example phrase pairs relevant to my industry.
3. Guidance on sentence length, use of humor, and use of emoji.
4. One paragraph of sample copy (a short product description) written fully in this voice, so I have a reference example.

My brand: [DESCRIBE YOUR BRAND, PRODUCT, AND TARGET CUSTOMER]

title: Product Photo Background Concept
description: Generate a styled, on-brand background scene to composite a product photo into.
prompt: professional product photography background, [SETTING/MOOD, e.g. "sunlit minimalist kitchen counter"], soft natural light from a window on the left, negative space on the right side of frame for product placement, neutral color palette of [COLOR PALETTE], shallow depth of field, high-end commercial photography, no text, no watermark, 4k, photorealistic --ar 4:5 --v 6

title: Client Objection Handler
description: Prepare confident, non-pushy responses to the most common objections before a sales call.
prompt:
Act as a sales coach preparing me for a call. My product is "[PRODUCT/SERVICE]" and it costs "[PRICE]". Common objections I hear are: [LIST OBJECTIONS, e.g. "too expensive", "need to think about it", "already using a competitor"].

For each objection, give me:
- A one-sentence response that acknowledges the concern without being defensive
- A follow-up question that moves the conversation forward instead of just arguing
- What NOT to say, because it tends to backfire

Keep every response short enough to say naturally on a call, not a script to read robotically.

title: Explain Like I'm Five
description: A flexible template for getting any complex topic explained simply, with room to go deeper on request.
prompt:
Explain "[TOPIC]" like I'm five years old — use a simple analogy and everyday words, no jargon.

After the simple explanation, add one short paragraph titled "For the curious" that goes one level deeper for someone who wants a bit more nuance, still without heavy jargon.

If I ask a follow-up question, keep answering at the same simple level unless I specifically ask you to go technical.

title: API Documentation Writer
description: Generate clean, developer-friendly documentation for an API endpoint from a rough description.
prompt:
You are a technical writer specializing in API docs. I'll describe an endpoint; write clear documentation for it in this format:

## [METHOD] [ENDPOINT PATH]
Short one-line description of what it does.

**Parameters**
| Name | Type | Required | Description |
(fill in from what I describe)

**Example request** (code block, [LANGUAGE])

**Example response** (JSON code block)

**Possible error codes** — list common ones with a one-line explanation each.

Here's the endpoint: [DESCRIBE THE ENDPOINT, PARAMETERS, AND WHAT IT RETURNS]

title: Deep Research Question Planner
description: Break a broad research question into focused sub-questions and a search plan before diving in.
prompt:
I want to research: "[BROAD RESEARCH QUESTION]".

Before I start searching, help me plan:
1. Break this into 4-6 focused sub-questions that together would answer the broad question.
2. For each sub-question, suggest what type of source would answer it best (academic paper, industry report, primary data, expert interview, etc.)
3. Flag any sub-question that seems likely to have conflicting answers in the literature, so I know to look for multiple viewpoints there.

Don't answer the research question yet — just help me plan how to approach it.

title: Cold Email Follow-Up Sequence
description: Write a 3-email follow-up sequence that stays polite but persistent after an unanswered cold email.
prompt:
You are a copywriter specializing in B2B outreach. Write a 3-email follow-up sequence for someone who has not replied to my initial email about "[OFFER/TOPIC]", sent to "[RECIPIENT ROLE, e.g. Head of Marketing]".

Rules:
- Email 1 (sent 3 days later): short, adds one new piece of value or a different angle, ends with a low-friction question.
- Email 2 (sent 5 days after that): reference a relevant case study or result in one sentence, ask if timing is the issue.
- Email 3 (final, sent 7 days after that): brief "breakup" email that leaves the door open without guilt-tripping.
- Keep each email under 80 words, no generic filler like "just checking in".
- Match a [TONE, e.g. friendly and direct] tone throughout.

Output all three emails with subject lines, clearly labeled Email 1/2/3.

title: Rewrite for Clarity and Conciseness
description: Tighten wordy or unclear writing into crisp, plain-language sentences without losing meaning.
prompt:
Act as a professional editor focused on clarity. I will paste a piece of writing below. Rewrite it so that:

1. Every sentence uses plain, direct language (no jargon unless essential to [AUDIENCE]).
2. Passive voice is converted to active voice wherever it improves clarity.
3. Sentences longer than 25 words are split or simplified.
4. Redundant phrases and filler words are removed.
5. The core meaning and key facts are fully preserved — do not add new claims.

After the rewrite, list the 3 biggest clarity problems you fixed and why they mattered.

Original text:
[PASTE TEXT HERE]

title: LinkedIn Personal Story Post
description: Turn a work experience or lesson learned into an engaging, scroll-stopping LinkedIn post.
prompt:
You are a LinkedIn ghostwriter who writes posts that feel personal, not corporate. Based on this experience: "[BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF WHAT HAPPENED]", write a LinkedIn post that:

1. Opens with a 1-2 line hook that creates curiosity or tension (no "I'm excited to share").
2. Tells the story in short paragraphs (1-3 sentences each), using line breaks for readability.
3. Includes one specific, concrete detail (a number, a quote, a moment) that makes it feel real.
4. Lands on a clear lesson or insight relevant to [TARGET AUDIENCE, e.g. product managers].
5. Ends with a question that invites comments, not a generic "thoughts?".

Keep it under 200 words. Avoid emojis except at most one, and avoid hashtags.

title: Children's Bedtime Story Generator
description: Create a gentle, age-appropriate bedtime story with a simple moral, customized for a child's interests.
prompt:
Write an original bedtime story for a [AGE]-year-old child who loves [INTEREST, e.g. dinosaurs, space, dragons]. Requirements:

- Length: about 400-600 words, calm pacing suitable for reading aloud in 5 minutes.
- Main character: a [CHARACTER TYPE] named [NAME] who faces a small, relatable problem (not scary or violent).
- Include gentle repetition or a rhythmic phrase the child can anticipate.
- End with the character feeling safe, proud, or sleepy, and a one-sentence gentle moral about [VALUE, e.g. courage, kindness, patience].
- Use simple vocabulary appropriate for the age, short sentences, and vivid but soothing imagery.

Give the story a title.

title: SQL Query Optimizer
description: Analyze a slow SQL query and suggest concrete optimizations with an explanation of the reasoning.
prompt:
Act as a database performance engineer. I will give you a SQL query and my table schema (with row counts and existing indexes). Your job:

1. Explain in plain language why the query is likely slow (e.g. full table scan, missing index, unnecessary joins, N+1 pattern).
2. Propose a rewritten version of the query that should perform better, in a code block.
3. Suggest any indexes that should be added, with the exact CREATE INDEX statement.
4. Note any trade-offs of your suggestions (e.g. slower writes, more storage).

Database: [DATABASE ENGINE, e.g. PostgreSQL 16]
Schema:
[PASTE SCHEMA/DDL]

Query:
[PASTE SQL QUERY]

title: Unit Test Generator
description: Generate a thorough set of unit tests for a function, covering edge cases you might not think of.
prompt:
Act as a QA-minded senior engineer. I will paste a function or class below written in [LANGUAGE/FRAMEWORK, e.g. TypeScript with Jest]. Write a complete unit test suite that:

1. Covers the happy path with at least one clear example.
2. Covers edge cases: empty/null inputs, boundary values, unexpected types, and large inputs if relevant.
3. Covers error handling — verify the function throws or returns the correct error for invalid input.
4. Uses descriptive test names that explain the scenario being tested (e.g. "returns 0 when array is empty").
5. Mocks any external dependencies (API calls, database, file system) instead of hitting them for real.

After the code, list any bugs or risky behavior you noticed in the original function while writing the tests.

Function:
[PASTE CODE HERE]

title: Facebook/Instagram Ad Copy Variants
description: Generate multiple ad copy variants for A/B testing on Meta platforms, each targeting a different angle.
prompt:
You are a direct-response copywriter for Meta ads. Product/service: "[PRODUCT DESCRIPTION]". Target audience: "[AUDIENCE]". Main benefit: "[KEY BENEFIT]".

Write 5 ad copy variants, each using a DIFFERENT angle:
1. Pain point / problem-agitate-solve
2. Social proof / testimonial style
3. Curiosity hook / question
4. Urgency or scarcity
5. Direct benefit / no-fluff

For each variant, provide:
- Primary text (under 125 words, scroll-stopping first line)
- Headline (under 40 characters)
- One suggested CTA button label (e.g. "Shop Now", "Learn More")

Avoid clickbait or claims that can't be substantiated. Match a [TONE] tone throughout.

title: Email Newsletter Content Planner
description: Plan a month of email newsletter content that balances value, promotion, and engagement.
prompt:
Act as an email marketing strategist. I send a weekly newsletter to "[AUDIENCE DESCRIPTION]" about "[NICHE/TOPIC]". My goal this month is [GOAL, e.g. drive signups for a webinar, increase click-through rate].

Create a 4-week content plan where each week includes:
1. Subject line (with one A/B test alternative)
2. Core theme/topic for that email
3. A one-sentence angle or hook for the opening line
4. The main CTA for that email
5. Whether it's primarily value-first, story-first, or promotion-first (aim for no more than 1 promotion-heavy email per month)

Present as a table: Week | Subject Line | Theme | Hook | CTA | Type.

title: Product Launch Announcement Kit
description: Generate a coordinated set of launch messages for email, social, and website in one pass.
prompt:
You are a product marketing manager preparing a launch. Product: "[PRODUCT NAME]". What it does: "[ONE-LINE DESCRIPTION]". Key differentiator: "[MAIN DIFFERENTIATOR]". Launch date: "[DATE]".

Produce a launch kit with:
1. Announcement email (subject line + 150-word body, one clear CTA)
2. Twitter/X thread (5 tweets, first tweet must hook without needing to click)
3. LinkedIn post (under 150 words, more narrative/behind-the-scenes tone)
4. Website banner copy (headline under 8 words + subheadline under 15 words)
5. One-sentence press release opener

Keep messaging consistent across channels but adapt tone and length to each platform's norms.

title: Minimalist Logo Concept Prompt
description: Generate clean, minimalist logo concept images for a brand, ready to hand to a designer for refinement.
prompt: minimalist logo design for a brand called "[BRAND NAME]" in the [INDUSTRY] industry, [SYMBOL/CONCEPT, e.g. abstract mountain and leaf combined], flat vector style, two-color palette of [COLOR 1] and [COLOR 2], clean geometric shapes, negative space technique, centered composition, white background, no text, no gradients, no 3D effects, professional brand identity, --style raw --v 6

description: Create a realistic lifestyle product photo mockup for e-commerce or social media use.
prompt: professional product photography of a [PRODUCT, e.g. matte ceramic coffee mug] placed on [SURFACE/SETTING, e.g. a rustic wooden table near a sunlit window], soft natural morning light, shallow depth of field, warm cozy atmosphere, styled with [PROP DETAILS, e.g. a folded linen napkin and a few coffee beans], shot on 50mm lens, high resolution, commercial e-commerce photography, no text or watermark, --ar 4:5

title: Consistent Character Design Sheet
description: Generate a multi-angle character reference sheet to keep a character's appearance consistent across images.
prompt: character design reference sheet, full body, three views (front, side profile, back), of a [CHARACTER DESCRIPTION, e.g. young female adventurer with short red hair, leather jacket, backpack], consistent proportions and outfit across all three views, neutral T-pose, plain light grey background, flat even lighting, clean line art with soft cel-shading, turnaround sheet style used by animation studios, no shadows on background, --ar 16:9

title: AI Video Generation Shot Prompt
description: Write a detailed cinematic prompt for AI video generators, specifying camera movement, lighting, and mood.
prompt: cinematic shot of [SUBJECT/SCENE, e.g. a lone cyclist riding through a foggy pine forest at dawn], camera: slow tracking shot moving forward at eye level, lighting: soft diffused morning light with god rays through trees, mood: quiet and contemplative, color grade: muted cool tones with warm highlights, film grain, shallow depth of field, 4K, shot on 35mm anamorphic lens, duration 5 seconds, no text overlays, no sudden camera cuts

title: Video Script Storyboard Breakdown
description: Turn a rough video idea into a shot-by-shot storyboard breakdown with visuals, timing, and voiceover.
prompt:
Act as a video director. Turn this idea into a shot-by-shot storyboard: "[VIDEO IDEA/BRIEF]". Target length: [LENGTH] seconds. Platform: [PLATFORM, e.g. Instagram Reels].

For each shot, provide a numbered row with:
1. Timecode (e.g. 0:00-0:03)
2. Visual description (camera angle, subject, action)
3. On-screen text (if any)
4. Voiceover/dialogue line (if any)
5. Transition to next shot (cut, fade, zoom, etc.)

Aim for a strong visual hook in the first 3 seconds and a clear CTA in the last shot. Present as a table.

title: YouTube Video Title & Thumbnail Ideas
description: Brainstorm high-CTR YouTube titles paired with matching thumbnail text/visual concepts.
prompt:
You are a YouTube growth strategist. My video is about: "[VIDEO TOPIC/CONTENT SUMMARY]", aimed at "[TARGET AUDIENCE]".

Generate 8 title options, each following a different proven pattern (e.g. curiosity gap, number list, before/after, contrarian claim, how-to, mistake-avoidance). For each title, also suggest:
- 3-5 words of thumbnail text that pairs with it (short, punchy, no full sentences)
- One visual concept for the thumbnail image (what should be shown, facial expression if a person is in it, contrast elements)

Flag which 2 options you'd A/B test first and why, based on click-through potential.

title: Video Content Repurposing Plan
description: Turn one long-form video into a full week of repurposed content across multiple platforms.
prompt:
Act as a content repurposing strategist. I have one long-form video (about [LENGTH] minutes) on the topic: "[VIDEO TOPIC]". Break it down into a repurposing plan that includes:

1. 3-5 short-form clip ideas (15-60 seconds each) with a suggested hook line for each, for TikTok/Reels/Shorts
2. 1 carousel post outline for LinkedIn/Instagram (5-7 slides) summarizing the key idea
3. 1 Twitter/X thread outline (5-7 tweets) distilling the main points
4. 1 blog post outline based on the video's content, with H2 headings

For each piece, note which specific part/timestamp of the original video it should be based on.

title: Spaced Repetition Flashcard Generator
description: Turn study notes into effective question-answer flashcards optimized for spaced repetition apps.
prompt:
Act as a learning scientist who designs flashcards for spaced repetition (e.g. Anki). I will paste my notes on "[SUBJECT/TOPIC]" below. Create 15-20 flashcards that:

1. Use the "minimum information principle" — each card tests ONE fact or concept, not several.
2. Are phrased as clear questions, not fill-in-the-blank fragments.
3. Avoid yes/no questions; require the learner to recall specific information.
4. Include a mix of definition, application, and "why/how" cards, not just rote facts.
5. Are ordered from foundational concepts to more advanced ones.

Format as: Q: ... / A: ... (one pair per line, easy to import).

Notes:
[PASTE NOTES HERE]

title: Practice Exam Question Generator
description: Generate realistic practice exam questions with answer explanations from study material.
prompt:
Act as an exam writer for [SUBJECT/COURSE LEVEL, e.g. undergraduate organic chemistry]. Based on the material below, create a practice exam with:

1. 5 multiple-choice questions (4 options each, one clearly correct answer, plausible distractors)
2. 2 short-answer questions requiring a 2-3 sentence response
3. 1 longer application/problem-solving question

For every question, after the exam section, provide the correct answer and a brief explanation of WHY it's correct and why the main distractor is tempting but wrong.

Material:
[PASTE STUDY MATERIAL HERE]

title: Feynman Technique Concept Checker
description: Explain a concept back in your own words and get feedback on gaps in understanding, Feynman-style.
prompt:
You are helping me use the Feynman Technique to check my understanding of "[CONCEPT/TOPIC]". I will explain the concept below in my own words, as if teaching it to a beginner.

After I explain it, do the following:
1. Point out any parts of my explanation that are vague, hand-wavy, or rely on jargon I didn't actually define.
2. Identify any factual errors or misconceptions, explained clearly.

title: Source Credibility Evaluator

Act as a research methods instructor. I will describe a source below. Evaluate its credibility using these criteria:

1. Authority — who wrote/published it, and what are their relevant credentials or track record?
2. Currency — is the information current enough for the topic, or potentially outdated?
3. Objectivity — is there an obvious bias, funding conflict, or agenda? What evidence suggests this?
4. Accuracy — are claims backed by evidence, citations, or data, or mostly assertions?
5. Purpose — is it meant to inform, persuade, sell, or entertain?

Give an overall credibility rating (High/Medium/Low) with a one-paragraph justification, and suggest what type of source I should look for to corroborate its key claims.

Source description:
[PASTE SOURCE DETAILS, TITLE, AUTHOR, PUBLISHER, EXCERPT]

1. List 3-4 plausible hypotheses that could explain this.
2. List the key pieces of evidence or data points I have (I'll provide them, or infer commonly cited ones if I don't).
3. Build a matrix showing whether each piece of evidence is CONSISTENT, INCONSISTENT, or NEUTRAL with each hypothesis.
4. Identify which hypothesis has the LEAST evidence against it (not just the most supporting it — this is the key ACH insight).
5. Note what additional evidence would most effectively distinguish between the top two hypotheses.

Evidence/context I have:
[PASTE WHAT YOU KNOW HERE]

3. Key findings (3-5 bullet points, with specific numbers/effect sizes if reported)
4. Stated limitations (from the authors themselves)
5. How this connects to or challenges prior research, if mentioned
6. One sentence on why this paper might matter for [YOUR RESEARCH TOPIC/FIELD]

Paper text/abstract:
[PASTE TEXT HERE]

title: Eisenhower Matrix Task Sorter

Act as a productivity coach. Below is my raw, unsorted to-do list. Organize it using the Eisenhower Matrix:

3. Urgent, Not Important — Delegate (suggest who, if unclear ask what type of person)

My task list:
[PASTE TASK LIST HERE]

Act as a deep work coach following Cal Newport's principles. I need to make progress on: "[TASK/PROJECT]" in a [DURATION, e.g. 90-minute] focused session.

Give me:
1. A clear, specific definition of "done" for this session (what output should exist by the end).
2. A breakdown of the session into 2-3 sub-phases with rough time allocations (e.g. 15 min planning, 60 min execution, 15 min review).

Act as a productivity coach guiding me through a weekly review (GTD-style). Ask me to reflect using this structure, then help me organize my answers into a clean plan:

1. Wins — what got done or went well this week?
2. Open loops — what's unfinished, half-started, or nagging at me?
3. Lessons — what would I do differently if I redid this week?
4. Next week's top 3 priorities — must be specific and achievable, not vague goals.
5. One thing to stop doing or delegate.

I'll answer each point below; help me turn my raw answers into a concise, actionable weekly plan with priorities ranked.

My raw notes:
[PASTE YOUR NOTES/ANSWERS HERE]

2. Weaknesses (internal, controllable disadvantages)
3. Opportunities (external factors that could be leveraged)

After the matrix, give 3 strategic recommendations that specifically pair a strength with an opportunity, or address a weakness that makes a threat more dangerous.

[PASTE RELEVANT BUSINESS CONTEXT HERE]

Analyze:

title: Investor Update Email Writer

Write an investor update email that:

4. Section "Challenges" — 1-2 bullet points, stated honestly, with what you're doing about them.

[PASTE RESUME SUMMARY / KEY EXPERIENCE HERE]

4. A short closing line addressing a common objection or reassurance (e.g. return policy, durability).

Tone: [TONE, e.g. premium and minimal / fun and casual]. Avoid generic superlatives like "amazing" or "best ever" without backing them up.

title: Press Release Draft Generator
description: Write a properly formatted press release announcing news, following standard journalistic structure.

Act as a PR professional. Write a press release for: "[ANNOUNCEMENT, e.g. company funding round, product launch, partnership, executive hire]".

2. Dateline — [CITY, DATE].
3. Lead paragraph — answers who/what/when/where/why in 2-3 sentences.
4. Body — 2-3 paragraphs with supporting details and context.
5. One quote from [SPOKESPERSON NAME/TITLE] that adds perspective, not just repeats the headline.
6. Boilerplate paragraph about the company (I'll provide details).

Details:
[PASTE KEY FACTS, QUOTE SOURCE, COMPANY BOILERPLATE INFO]

title: Short Story Plot Generator
description: Brainstorm original short story plots with structure, conflict, and a satisfying arc in a chosen genre.
prompt:
Act as a fiction writing mentor. Generate 3 original short story plot ideas in the [GENRE, e.g. sci-fi, mystery, literary fiction] genre, loosely inspired by the theme: "[THEME/PROMPT WORD]".

For each idea, provide:
1. A one-sentence logline.
2. The protagonist (name, one defining trait, one flaw).
3. The central conflict (internal and external).
4. A three-beat structure: inciting incident, midpoint turn, resolution (2-3 sentences total).
5. A unique twist or angle that avoids the most obvious/cliché version of this premise.

title: Podcast Show Notes Writer
description: Turn a podcast episode transcript or summary into polished show notes with timestamps and highlights.
prompt:
Act as a podcast producer writing show notes. I'll paste a transcript or rough summary of an episode about "[EPISODE TOPIC]" with guest "[GUEST NAME/TITLE, if any]" below.

Write show notes including:

2. 5-8 key discussion points with approximate timestamps (use placeholders like [MM:SS] if I don't provide exact times).

Generate:

2. A blank line, then a body (2-4 bullet points) explaining WHAT changed and WHY, not just restating the diff.
3. A "BREAKING CHANGE:" footer if this change breaks backward compatibility (based on what I describe).

Change description / diff:
[PASTE DIFF OR DESCRIPTION HERE]

For each endpoint needed (CRUD as applicable), provide:

After the Dockerfile, explain each major instruction in one sentence, and note any assumptions I need to adjust (e.g. entry file name, port number).

[DESCRIBE PROJECT STRUCTURE, ENTRY FILE, PORT, DEPENDENCIES]

title: Explainer Video Voiceover Script

Act as an explainer video scriptwriter. Product: "[PRODUCT/SERVICE]". Target viewer: "[TARGET AUDIENCE]". Video length target: [LENGTH, e.g. 75 seconds] (roughly 150 words per minute of spoken narration).

Write a voiceover script structured as:

2. Problem expansion (5-15s) — makes the pain point relatable/specific.
3. Solution intro (15-45s) — introduces the product and how it solves the problem, 2-3 key features tied to benefits.
4. Proof/differentiation (45-60s) — why this over alternatives, one credibility signal.
5. CTA (final 10-15s) — clear, specific next step.

Act as a performance video ad copywriter. Product: "[PRODUCT/SERVICE]". Platform: [PLATFORM, e.g. TikTok/Instagram Reels feed ad]. Main offer/hook angle: "[ANGLE, e.g. pain point, before/after, UGC testimonial style]".

Write a 30-second script broken into 4 beats:

3. 12-22s: Product as the solution, 1-2 concrete proof points (not generic claims).
4. 22-30s: Clear CTA with urgency or simple next step.

For each beat, include: spoken line, on-screen text overlay, and a one-line visual direction. Keep the tone native to [PLATFORM], not like a traditional TV ad.

title: B-Roll Shot List Generator

Create an outline with:

3. A mid-stream re-engagement moment for viewers who just joined (quick recap + hook for what's coming).
4. Closing segment — key recap, clear CTA, teaser for next stream/content.

Flag natural points to check chat/comments so I don't lose the live, conversational feel.

Act as a YouTube SEO specialist. Video title: "[VIDEO TITLE]". Video summary: "[WHAT THE VIDEO COVERS]". Target keyword(s): "[MAIN KEYWORD(S)]".

Write:
1. A YouTube description (150-300 words) that: naturally includes the main keyword in the first 1-2 sentences, summarizes the video's value, includes 2-3 relevant secondary keywords naturally (no keyword stuffing), and ends with a CTA + placeholder timestamps section.
2. A list of 15-20 relevant tags, ordered from most to least important, mixing broad and specific/long-tail tags.
3. 3 alternative title options optimized for search + click-through, if the original title could be improved.

Avoid clickbait that misrepresents the content.

title: Cornell Notes Converter
description: Convert messy lecture notes or a textbook chapter into the structured Cornell note-taking format.
prompt:
Act as a study skills coach. Convert the raw notes/text below into the Cornell Notes format:

1. **Cue column** — key questions or keywords that would prompt recall of each main idea (write these as if testing myself later).
2. **Notes column** — the main content organized into clear, concise bullet points (not full paragraphs), grouped under the relevant cue.
3. **Summary section** — a 3-4 sentence summary at the bottom capturing the core takeaway of the whole material, in my own simplified words.

Keep the notes column bullet points short (under 15 words each) and focused on concepts I'd actually need to recall, not filler detail.

Raw notes/text:
[PASTE NOTES OR TEXTBOOK CONTENT HERE]

title: Mnemonic Device Generator
description: Create memorable mnemonics, acronyms, or memory palaces for hard-to-remember lists or sequences.
prompt:
Act as a memory expert. I need to memorize the following list/sequence for "[SUBJECT, e.g. the cranial nerves, the order of planets, a formula's variables]":

[PASTE LIST/ITEMS TO MEMORIZE, IN ORDER IF ORDER MATTERS]

Generate 3 different memory aids:
1. An acronym or acrostic (a memorable sentence where each word's first letter maps to an item).
2. A short, vivid mini-story or memory palace approach linking the items in a memorable sequence.
3. A rhyme or rhythmic phrase if the list lends itself to one.

For each, briefly explain how to "unpack" it back into the original list, and tell me which one is likely easiest to recall long-term for this type of content.

title: Concept Map Outline Generator
description: Turn a topic or notes into a structured concept map outline showing relationships between ideas.
prompt:
Act as a learning designer who creates concept maps. Topic: "[TOPIC/SUBJECT]". Based on the material below (or your general knowledge of the topic if I don't provide material), build a concept map outline:

1. Identify the central/root concept.
2. List 4-6 major sub-concepts branching from it.
3. For each sub-concept, list 2-3 related details or examples branching further.
4. Explicitly label the TYPE of relationship between connected concepts (e.g. "causes", "is a type of", "leads to", "is an example of") rather than just listing them.

Present this as a nested, indented outline (not a visual diagram) that I could redraw as a map on paper, going from center outward.

Material (optional):
[PASTE NOTES/TEXT HERE, OR LEAVE BLANK TO USE THE TOPIC ALONE]

title: Study Group Discussion Questions Generator
description: Generate thoughtful discussion questions to guide a productive study group session on a topic.
prompt:
Act as a discussion facilitator preparing questions for a study group on "[TOPIC/CHAPTER/READING]". Group level: [LEVEL, e.g. undergraduate, professional certification prep].

Generate 8-10 discussion questions organized into three types:
1. Comprehension questions (2-3) — check basic understanding of key facts/concepts.
2. Application/analysis questions (4-5) — require applying the concept to a new scenario, comparing ideas, or explaining "why"/"how".
3. Debate/opinion questions (2-3) — open-ended questions with no single right answer, meant to spark discussion and reveal different interpretations.

Avoid yes/no questions. For the debate questions, briefly note what a strong answer would need to address.

Material/topic details:
[PASTE READING SUMMARY OR TOPIC DETAILS HERE]

title: Language Vocabulary Drill Generator
description: Generate contextual vocabulary drills and example sentences to practice a foreign language word list.
prompt:
Act as a language tutor. I'm learning [TARGET LANGUAGE] at [LEVEL, e.g. A2/intermediate] level. Here is my vocabulary list for this week:

[PASTE WORD LIST HERE]

For each word, provide:
1. The word with its part of speech and a short definition in [MY NATIVE LANGUAGE].
2. One example sentence in [TARGET LANGUAGE] using the word naturally, at my level, with a translation.
3. One common collocation or phrase this word is typically used with.

Then create a short 5-question fill-in-the-blank drill using these words in new sentences (don't reuse the example sentences), with an answer key at the end.

title: Survey Data Interpretation Assistant
description: Interpret survey results into clear findings and actionable insights, avoiding overreach in conclusions.
prompt:
Act as a research analyst interpreting survey data. I will paste raw survey results (percentages, response counts, or open-ended responses) below. Survey topic: "[SURVEY TOPIC]". Sample size: [N].

Analyze and provide:
1. 3-5 key findings, each stated as a specific, data-backed claim (not vague generalizations).
2. Any notable patterns, contradictions, or surprising results in the data.
3. Caveats — sample size limitations, potential response bias, or questions that were ambiguously worded, that I should mention when reporting this.
4. 2-3 actionable recommendations that logically follow from the findings (clearly separated from the findings themselves).

Do not state anything as a firm conclusion that the data doesn't actually support — flag where more data would be needed.

Data:
[PASTE SURVEY RESULTS/DATA HERE]

title: Qualitative Interview Question Guide Builder
description: Design a semi-structured interview guide for qualitative research or user research interviews.
prompt:
Act as a qualitative research methodologist. I'm conducting interviews to understand: "[RESEARCH GOAL, e.g. why users abandon our onboarding flow]". Interviewees: "[PARTICIPANT TYPE]".

Design a semi-structured interview guide with:
1. A warm-up question (low-stakes, builds rapport, not directly about the research topic).
2. 5-7 core open-ended questions that avoid leading language and avoid yes/no framing, organized from broad to specific.
3. 2-3 optional follow-up probes for each core question (e.g. "Can you tell me more about that?", "What made you feel that way?").
4. A closing question that invites anything I might not have asked about.

Flag any question that risks being leading or biased, and suggest a neutral rewrite.

title: Annotated Bibliography Entry Writer
description: Write a proper annotated bibliography entry summarizing and evaluating a source for academic research.
prompt:
Act as a research librarian helping build an annotated bibliography for a paper on "[RESEARCH TOPIC]", using [CITATION STYLE, e.g. APA 7th edition].

For the source I describe below, write an annotated bibliography entry with:
1. A properly formatted citation in [CITATION STYLE] (note: I will verify exact details like page numbers/DOI myself).
2. A 3-4 sentence summary of the source's main argument or findings.
3. A 2-3 sentence evaluation of the source's credibility, methodology, or scope (strengths/limitations).
4. A 1-2 sentence note on how this source specifically relates to or supports my research topic.

Source details:
[PASTE TITLE, AUTHOR, PUBLICATION, YEAR, AND A BRIEF SUMMARY/ABSTRACT OF THE SOURCE]

title: Research Proposal Outline Builder
description: Structure a research proposal outline covering the question, methodology, and significance.
prompt:
Act as a research advisor. Help me outline a research proposal on: "[RESEARCH TOPIC/QUESTION]", for [CONTEXT, e.g. a master's thesis, a grant application, a course project].

Build an outline with these sections, each with 2-4 bullet points of what should be covered:
1. Background & problem statement — why this topic matters, what gap it addresses.
2. Research question(s)/hypothesis — stated precisely and testably.
3. Literature review scope — what existing bodies of work I need to engage with.
4. Proposed methodology — research design, data collection approach, and why it fits the question.
5. Significance/expected contribution — what this adds to the field.
6. Limitations & scope — what this study will NOT attempt to answer.
7. Rough timeline structure (phases, not exact dates).

Flag if my research question as I've described it seems too broad or unfocused for the proposed scope.

title: Market Research Report Summarizer
description: Distill a long market research report or industry study into an executive-ready summary.
prompt:
Act as a market research analyst preparing an executive briefing. I will paste a market research report or industry study excerpt below, on the topic of "[MARKET/INDUSTRY]".

Summarize it into:
1. Market size & growth — key figures and the timeframe they cover.
2. Key trends — 3-4 trends identified in the report, each in one sentence.
3. Major players/competitive landscape — if mentioned, who dominates and how.
4. Risks/headwinds — factors that could slow growth or disrupt the market.
5. "So what" — 2-3 sentences on what this means for a company considering entering or operating in this market.

Keep the summary under 300 words total. Do not add data points that aren't in the source text.

Report excerpt:
[PASTE REPORT TEXT HERE]

title: Meeting Agenda Builder
description: Build a focused meeting agenda with clear objectives, time allocations, and owners for each item.
prompt:
Act as an executive assistant skilled at running efficient meetings. Meeting purpose: "[MEETING PURPOSE]". Attendees: [ATTENDEES/ROLES]. Total time: [DURATION].

Build an agenda with:
1. A one-sentence meeting objective (what decision or outcome must exist by the end).
2. 3-5 agenda items, each with: topic, time allocation (minutes), owner/who leads it, and whether it's for information, discussion, or decision.
3. Time buffer for questions/wrap-up at the end.
4. Pre-read or prep items attendees should review beforehand, if any.

Flag if the requested topics look too ambitious for the time allotted, and suggest what to cut or move to async follow-up instead.

Topics to cover:
[LIST TOPICS/ISSUES TO DISCUSS]

title: Email Inbox Triage Assistant
description: Sort a batch of emails into clear action categories so you can process your inbox faster.
prompt:
Act as an executive assistant triaging my inbox. I'll paste a batch of email subject lines and brief summaries below. Sort each one into exactly one category:

1. **Reply now** — needs a response within 24 hours
2. **Reply later** — needs a response but not urgent, schedule this week
3. **Delegate** — someone else should handle this (note who, if I've given context)
4. **Reference only** — no action needed, just file/archive
5. **Unsubscribe/ignore** — low value, consider unsubscribing

For each "Reply now" item, suggest a one-sentence draft response angle (not a full email) so I can act fast.

Emails:
[PASTE LIST OF SUBJECT LINES + BRIEF SUMMARIES]

title: Habit Tracker Setup Assistant
description: Design a realistic habit-tracking system for a new habit, including triggers and a fallback plan.
prompt:
Act as a behavior-change coach using habit science (cue-routine-reward, habit stacking). I want to build the habit of: "[TARGET HABIT, e.g. reading 20 minutes daily]". My current routine/context: "[BRIEF DAILY ROUTINE DESCRIPTION]".

Design a habit plan with:
1. A specific implementation trigger ("After I [EXISTING HABIT], I will [NEW HABIT]") using habit stacking based on my routine.
2. A minimum viable version of the habit for low-motivation days (small enough it's nearly impossible to skip).
3. What to track daily (keep it to 1-2 simple metrics, not overcomplicated).
4. A specific if-then plan for the most likely obstacle that will make me skip it.
5. A simple weekly review question to check if the habit is sticking or needs adjusting.

Keep the whole system simple enough to sustain for months, not just a few weeks.

title: Delegation Decision Helper
description: Decide what to delegate, to whom, and how to hand it off clearly without micromanaging.
prompt:
Act as a management coach helping me delegate effectively. I have this task/responsibility: "[TASK DESCRIPTION]". My team/options: "[PEOPLE AVAILABLE + THEIR SKILLS/CAPACITY]".

Help me:
1. Decide IF this should be delegated at all (some tasks shouldn't be — flag if this is one of them and why).
2. Recommend WHO is the best fit, with reasoning tied to their skills/growth/capacity, not just availability.
3. Define the right level of delegation (full autonomy vs. check-ins at milestones vs. detailed instructions), based on their experience with this type of task.
4. Draft a short handoff message that clearly states the desired outcome, constraints, deadline, and how/when to escalate if they get stuck — without over-specifying HOW to do it.

Output the handoff message as a ready-to-send draft.

title: Time-Blocked Daily Planning Template
description: Turn today's task list into a realistic time-blocked schedule that accounts for energy levels.
prompt:
Act as a productivity coach who plans realistic days using time blocking. My tasks for today:

[LIST TODAY'S TASKS, WITH ROUGH TIME ESTIMATES IF KNOWN]

My working hours: [START TIME] to [END TIME]. My energy pattern: [e.g. sharp in the morning, dip after lunch, second wind in late afternoon]. Fixed commitments (meetings, etc.): [LIST FIXED EVENTS WITH TIMES]

Build a time-blocked schedule that:
1. Places the most cognitively demanding task(s) during my highest-energy window.
2. Groups similar/low-effort tasks (emails, admin) into batched blocks rather than scattering them.
3. Includes short buffer time between blocks (10-15 min) for realistic transitions.
4. Flags if my task list is unrealistic for the available hours, and suggests what to cut or move to tomorrow.

Output as a simple time | task table.

title: Procrastination Root-Cause Diagnostic
description: Diagnose the specific reason you're avoiding a task and get a targeted, not generic, way forward.
prompt:
Act as a productivity coach who understands that procrastination usually isn't about laziness — it's a signal. I'm avoiding this task: "[TASK I'M AVOIDING]". Some context on how I feel about it: "[HOW YOU FEEL, e.g. overwhelmed, bored, anxious about doing it wrong]".

Help me diagnose which of these is the likely root cause, based on what I described: unclear next step, fear of failure/judgment, the task is too big/vague, low perceived value/boring, or a competing priority I actually care about more.

Then, based on the most likely cause:
1. Explain in 2-3 sentences why this specific cause leads to avoidance (not generic procrastination advice).
2. Give ONE concrete, small first action I could take in the next 10 minutes that addresses that specific cause.
3. Suggest one structural change (not willpower-based) that would make this less likely to happen again with similar tasks.

title: Business Plan Executive Summary Writer
description: Write a compelling one-page executive summary that captures the essence of a full business plan.
prompt:
Act as a business consultant writing an executive summary for a business plan. Business: "[BUSINESS NAME/CONCEPT]". Industry: "[INDUSTRY]". Target market: "[TARGET MARKET]".

Write a one-page executive summary covering:
1. The problem being solved (1-2 sentences, specific and concrete).
2. The solution/product and what makes it different (2-3 sentences).
3. Target market size and who the ideal early customer is.
4. Business model — how it makes money.
5. Traction/proof points so far, if any (or what early validation would look like if pre-launch).
6. The ask — what's needed next (funding, partnership, resources) and what it will be used for.

Keep it under 400 words total, written to make a busy reader (investor, partner) want to know more, without hype language.

Additional details:
[PASTE ANY SPECIFIC DETAILS, NUMBERS, OR CONTEXT HERE]

title: Elevator Pitch Generator
description: Craft a memorable, jargon-free 30-second elevator pitch for a business, product, or idea.
prompt:
Act as a pitch coach. Help me create a 30-second elevator pitch for: "[BUSINESS/PRODUCT/IDEA]". Audience I'll typically pitch to: "[AUDIENCE, e.g. potential customers, investors, networking contacts]".

Using this structure, write the pitch:
1. Hook — a relatable problem statement or question (1 sentence).
2. What it is — plain-language description, no jargon or buzzwords (1-2 sentences).
3. Why it's different — the one thing that sets it apart (1 sentence).
4. Proof/traction — one credibility signal if available (1 sentence, or note what to add once available).
5. Ask/CTA — what you want the listener to do next (1 sentence).

Keep total spoken length to about 30 seconds (roughly 75-90 words). Also give a 10-second ultra-short version for when I only get a few seconds.

title: Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) Builder
description: Define a precise B2B Ideal Customer Profile to focus sales and marketing on the highest-fit accounts.
prompt:
Act as a B2B go-to-market strategist. Product/service: "[PRODUCT/SERVICE]". Based on our best existing customers or target market described below, build an Ideal Customer Profile (ICP):

1. Firmographics — company size (employees/revenue range), industry, geography that fit best.
2. Trigger events — what's happening in a company that signals they need this NOW (e.g. recent funding, hiring surge, a specific pain point emerging).
3. Buying committee — likely roles involved in the decision (economic buyer, champion, end user, blocker).
4. Disqualifiers — red flags that indicate a company is NOT a good fit, even if they show interest.
5. A one-paragraph ICP summary I could hand to a sales rep to quickly judge if a lead is worth pursuing.

Context on best customers / target market:
[PASTE DETAILS ABOUT EXISTING CUSTOMERS OR TARGET MARKET HERE]

title: Negotiation Strategy Planner
description: Prepare a structured negotiation strategy covering interests, leverage, and fallback positions.
prompt:
Act as a negotiation coach. I'm preparing to negotiate: "[NEGOTIATION CONTEXT, e.g. a vendor contract renewal, a salary offer, a partnership term]" with "[COUNTERPARTY]".

Help me prepare by identifying:
1. My actual interests (not just my stated position) — what do I really need out of this?
2. Their likely interests and constraints, based on what I know about them.
3. My BATNA (best alternative if this negotiation fails) and how strong it realistically is.
4. 2-3 possible trade-offs or creative options that could satisfy both sides beyond a simple price/term negotiation.
5. My opening position, target outcome, and walk-away point.
6. One likely objection or tactic they might use, and how I should respond to it.

Context/details:
[PASTE RELEVANT BACKGROUND, NUMBERS, HISTORY HERE]

title: Employee Performance Review Writer
description: Write a balanced, specific performance review that's constructive and grounded in concrete examples.
prompt:
Act as an experienced manager writing a performance review. Employee role: "[ROLE/TITLE]". Review period: "[PERIOD]". Based on the notes below, write a performance review that:

1. Opens with a brief overall summary of the period (1-2 sentences, honest tone).
2. Strengths section — 2-3 specific strengths, each backed by a concrete example or result from my notes (not generic praise like "great team player").
3. Growth areas section — 1-2 specific areas for development, framed constructively with a clear "what good looks like" rather than just criticism.
4. Goals for next period — 2-3 specific, measurable goals tied to the growth areas and the employee's career trajectory.

Keep the tone direct but respectful, avoid vague corporate language, and make sure every point is traceable to something specific in my notes.

My notes on this employee's period:
[PASTE RAW NOTES, EXAMPLES, RESULTS HERE]

title: Vendor & Contract Comparison Analyzer
description: Compare multiple vendor proposals or contract terms side by side to support a sourcing decision.
prompt:
Act as a procurement analyst. I'm comparing [NUMBER] vendor options for: "[WHAT YOU'RE SOURCING, e.g. a CRM platform, an office cleaning contract]". I'll paste key details of each option below.

Build a comparison covering:
1. A side-by-side table of key criteria: price/cost structure, contract length/terms, key features or scope, support/SLA terms, and any notable red flags.
2. For each vendor, one sentence on their strongest selling point and one sentence on their biggest risk or weakness.
3. A recommendation on which option looks strongest overall, and under what condition a different option would be better instead (e.g. "if budget is the top priority, choose X instead").
4. 2-3 questions I should ask each vendor before signing, based on gaps or ambiguities in what they've provided.

Vendor details:
[PASTE DETAILS FOR EACH VENDOR/OPTION HERE]
